facts.note: Some time before 1799, the siren was invented by the Scottish natural philosopher John Robison.

facts.claim: 오르간 파이프 일부를 울리는 악기로 사용
facts.note: Robison's sirens were used as musical instruments; specifically, they powered some of the pipes in an organ.
In 1819, an improved siren was developed and named by Baron Charles Cagniard de la Tour.
Robison's siren consisted of a stopcock that opened and closed a pneumatic tube.

facts.claim: 드 라 투르의 것 — 구멍 뚫린 원판 두 장, 하나는 고정 하나는 회전, 공기 흐름을 끊어 소리
facts.note: De la Tour's siren consisted of two perforated disks that were mounted coaxially at the outlet of a pneumatic tube. One disk was stationary, while the other disk rotated. The rotating disk periodically interrupted the flow of air through the fixed disk, producing a tone.

question.hintNote: In Germany and some other European countries, the pneumatic two-tone (hi-lo) siren consists of two sets of air horns, one high pitched and the other low pitched.
